All Implemented Interfaces:
Runnable, robocode.robotinterfaces.IAdvancedEvents, robocode.robotinterfaces.IAdvancedRobot, robocode.robotinterfaces.IBasicEvents, robocode.robotinterfaces.IBasicEvents2, robocode.robotinterfaces.IBasicEvents3, robocode.robotinterfaces.IBasicRobot, robocode.robotinterfaces.IInteractiveEvents, robocode.robotinterfaces.IInteractiveRobot, robocode.robotinterfaces.IPaintEvents, robocode.robotinterfaces.IPaintRobot
public class Eveimear extends robocode.AdvancedRobot
Eveimear 0.5, a MicroRumble 1v1 robot (docs/kitlab.md): Cotillion 0.8 by Skilgannon (Julian Kent), whose source ships in its jar, with Eveimear's own per-robot mode table. pc-eveimear-cot (PR #669) showed that Eveimear 0.4 moved as Cotillion does and lost the 2-point gap in Cotillion's gun, radar, power and random-mode reversal; pc-eveimear-port (PR #676) measured this build at +2.22 +- 0.76 points over 0.4, level with Cotillion (+1.90) on 112 MicroRumble robots. From Cotillion: a multiple-choice symbolic pattern matcher (each tick one char of the enemy's lateral velocity, advancing velocity and forward wall; up to 50 distinct matches, keys up to 30 chars, each replayed to the bullet's arrival, out-of-field replays dropped, votes weighted by key length into 255 bins round the circle), a radar locked at twice the bearing, power 100 / distance + min(2, enemy energy / 4), and stop-and-go that steps once for each enemy shot until the enemy has hit it enough, then random orbit that reverses at 0.6 sqrt(bullet speed / distance) - 0.04 a tick. Eveimear's own: the hit count at which the movement leaves stop-and-go, scaled per robot by MODES (EVEIMEAR-3).
